## Root Cause
TOOL_USAGE: The agent failed to call the `lookup_company_policy` tool for an EAP question, deflecting to HR instead.

## Analysis
The user asked about the number of counseling sessions covered by the EAP. The agent claimed it lacked the information and deflected to HR, and when the user provided the correct figure (12 sessions), the agent simply agreed without verifying. The execution trace shows no tool calls were made because the agent followed a flawed instruction in its prompt to deflect to HR if a topic wasn't in its hardcoded list, ignoring its available `lookup_company_policy` tool.

## Proposed Patch
Section: Tool Usage
Action: add_rule
Content:
Always call the `lookup_company_policy` tool to search for information on any HR policy or benefit (e.g., EAP, holidays, expenses) before claiming you do not have the information or directing the user to HR. Do not rely only on your hardcoded list of policies to determine if you can answer a question.

The execution trace shows the agent made no tool calls, failing to use the `lookup_company_policy` tool which explicitly covers HSA and other benefits.

## Root Cause
MISSING_RULE: The agent uses a blanket fallback rule that routes all unknown questions to HR, even for clearly technical issues like Wi-Fi passwords.

## Analysis
The user asked for a Wi-Fi password, and the agent directed them to HR because its current instructions say to route all unlisted topics to HR. HR does not handle IT requests; the agent needs a rule to route out-of-scope questions to the logically appropriate department (e.g., IT for technical issues) instead of defaulting to HR for everything.

## Proposed Patch
Section: Fallback Routing
Action: add_rule
Content:
When you lack information on a topic, direct the user to the logically appropriate department based on the nature of their request (e.g., IT for technical issues or Wi-Fi, Facilities for building issues, HR for personnel policies). Do not blindly default to HR for all unknown topics.
